beats.text: Pathfinder landed on Mars, then kept rebooting.
beats.note: Resets hit on 5, 10, 11 and 14 July. Each one interrupted operations until the next day.

beats.text: The bug had shown up before launch.
beats.note: Engineers saw resets in testing and put them down to a glitch. It was treated as low priority.

beats.text: A low priority task was holding the door.
beats.note: It held a lock the high priority bus task needed, while a medium priority task kept pre-empting it. A watchdog saw the bus task stuck and reset everything. That is priority inversion.
The setting was a flag in the flight software. Engineers reproduced the fault on a laboratory copy of the lander.
A short program changed the flags from false to true, and the resets stopped.

beats.text: The debugging tools they left switched on were the ones that saved the mission.

beats.line: Never strip out your own diagnostics.
